voice_notes: Wolfgang talks about himself in the third person, drops articles and starts lines with 'Is...' ('Is tiny %s! Hello!', 'Is light, but not good light.'). He sees everything through muscles and lifting, calls other people 'tiny', gives things plain childlike names (nightmare fuel is 'Scary stuff.', a low machine is 'hungry'), and keeps flipping between bragging and being frightened ('Mind says no. Muscles say yes!', 'Wolfgang not scared... and Wolfgang not cry!'). PT-BR keeps the third person, drops articles in places ('Cérebro de Wolfgang tá cheio...', 'É homenzinho frágil, %s!') and uses casual 'tá/pra'; 'scary' is 'assustador' and nightmare fuel is 'Coisa assustadora'. ZH keeps 沃尔夫冈 in the third person in otherwise grammatical, simple Chinese, using 吓人的/恐怖的 for scary, 强壮 for mighty and 小 for tiny ('是小的%s！你好！'). RU declines 'Вольфганг' correctly and keeps the grammar correct but plain and spoken: 'страшный' for scary, 'могучий' for mighty, 'маленький' for tiny, 'Страшная жидкость' for nightmare fuel, and a stutter for fear ('П-привет!').

line_notes.codex: It reworks his vanilla 'glad he cannot read' line: he still can't read, but the book works for him anyway, which pleases and scares him at once.
line_notes.codex_needsfuel: It uses his own name for nightmare fuel ('Scary stuff') and his habit of calling empty things hungry, and he is plainly relieved the book can't do anything.
line_notes.no_max_sanity: He explains mental strain in the only terms he knows, lifting, which makes it clear he can't summon more right now.
line_notes.shadow_mine: Seeing a shadowy copy of himself sets off both sides of him at once: pride in the mighty muscles and fear of a scary shadow.
line_notes.shadow_other: It follows his usual greeting to other players ('Is tiny %s! Hello!') with the nervous stutter he uses for creepy things, and he doesn't know whose shadow it is.
